candidates.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
candidates.abstract: As semiconductor device dimensions approach phonon mean free paths, heat transport enters ballistic and quasi-ballistic regimes where Fourier's law becomes inadequate. The phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) describes these nonequilibrium effects but presents significant computational challenges. This work introduces JAX-Nano, a GPU-accelerated, end-to-end differentiable phonon BTE solver for nanoscale heat transport. The solver integrates steady-state and transient BTE formulations within a unified finite-volume framework, supporting structured and unstructured meshes, mode-resolved transport, phonon scattering, volumetric heat generation, and multiple boundary conditions. Automatic differentiation enables gradient computation with respect to transport properties, boundary conditions, heat-generation rates, and geometric parameters without separately derived adjoint equations. Numerical predictions are validated against analytical solutions and established BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes. Applications to complex three-dimensional geometries are demonstrated using single-fin, double-fin, and arrayed fin field-effect transistor (FinFET) configurations. Gradie

candidates.title: Möbius Fusion Algebra
candidates.comment: 65 pages, many figures. Animated versions of the proofs of Propositions 4.23 and 5.6 are available at https://ippo0127.github.io/movies/mobius_prop4_23.html and https://ippo0127.github.io/movies/mobius_prop5_6.html
candidates.abstract: Given a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with an anti-monoidal involution $\mathsf{P}$, we define a generally non-commutative algebra from this data, which we call the Möbius fusion algebra $\mathfrak{M}$ of $(\mathcal{C},\mathsf{P})$, in terms of ribbon graphs drawn on the Möbius band, where the orientation-reversal of the Möbius band acts on the graphs by $\mathsf{P}$. We show that this algebra is semisimple, and give a formula for the dimensions of its simple modules, in terms of the modular $S$-matrix of $\mathcal{C}$ and a certain set of quantities extracted from the action of $\mathsf{P}$. This formula is expected to play the role of a non-orientable analogue of the Verlinde formula, in the context of Reshetikhin-Turaev-type topological quantum field theories on non-orientable manifolds.

candidates.title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
candidates.comment: 26 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to AJ
candidates.abstract: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. candidates.title: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
candidates.abstract: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions of the Universe that encode valuable information about its large-scale structure and evolution. By extending spherical voids into overlapping sphere structures, the Popcorn Void Finder demonstrated an improved statistical characterization of cosmic void populations. However, its origin as a research prototype progressively hindered its maintainability and extensibility. Moreover, post-publication algorithmic modifications have not been systematically evaluated, leaving their statistical and computational consequences insufficiently characterized. In this work, we present a comprehensive reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder, prioritizing algorithmic transparency, maintainability, and reproducibility. We document the complete identification procedure, revisit the original algorithmic choices, and evaluate their statistical and computational consequences. Comparisons between implementations revealed a significant change in the behavior of the Void Size Function, which is now characterized by a power-law regime transitioning to a Schechter-like distribution. These changes not only provide a better characterization of void sizes, but enabl

candidates.title: A high-speed and high-resolution 3D velocity map imaging system with a neuromorphic camera
candidates.abstract: An improved camera-based 3D-velocity map imaging (VMI) system was demonstrated with a neuromorphic camera. We show a machine vision event-driven camera can achieve an unprecedented latency of 2 microseconds when detecting single ion/electron with a microchannel plate imaging detector, which boosts the speed of the momentum imaging system to more than 100 kHz, while the system with a conventional frame camera is limited to a few kHz. The high spatial resolution of the camera offers additional performance boost while maintaining excellent multi-hit capability and a high time resolution.

candidates.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
candidates.abstract: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $γ= 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $δΦ_2 \propto a_b^2$. candidates.title: ESM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Whether AI Agents Understand Earth System Model Physics and Code
candidates.abstract: AI coding agents that modify Earth System Model (ESM) code must preserve both software interfaces and the physical assumptions encoded in them. We introduce ESM-Bench, a benchmark of 60 developer-commit tasks from 6 repositories: Noah-MP, CLM5, SUMMA, ParFlow, MOM6, and VIC. The v5 corpus contains 17 physics-based bug fixes, 16 process-representation modifications, 13 parameterization-scheme selections, and 14 parameter-optimization tasks. Each task includes a scientific objective, parent-commit source files, a reference diff, and three stored prompt variants. An artifact audit confirms that all 60 reference diffs apply to their supplied starting files. We define an eight-item patch-review rubric and audit five archived patch fixtures against the implemented local checkers. None of the five fixture diffs applies to its supplied starting files, yet three text-pattern checkers return a pass. A ParFlow expression replay disagrees with the reference slopes, and a MOM6 pattern check detects an omitted update. Inspection also identifies a retained VIC reference assignment that overwrites the intended vegetation-specific albedo. These findings expose limits of reference patches and local

candidates.title: The Thue-Morse route to chaos in the open quantum baker map
candidates.comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables; submitted to J. Phys. A; ancillary files: scripts and logs of the exact entropy certificates of appendix B
candidates.abstract: We study the resonances of the quantum baker map opened by a window of width $w$ centred at $q_c$. For $q_c=1/2$ the survivor set of the classical doubling map with a hole goes from zero to positive topological entropy along the Thue-Morse route, and we find numerically, for $N$ up to $2^{25}$, that the resonance spectrum follows this route step by step, also where the entropy is zero. Below the threshold $w_c=4a^*-1$, with $a^*$ the Thue-Morse constant, the surviving cycles have periods $2^ν$ and their thresholds accumulate doubly exponentially. Each cycle gives, as isolated orbits do, a multiplet of resonances close to modulus $2^{-1/2}$, with phases set by its action. Since a cycle is resolved only if its period is shorter than about $\log_2 N$, twice the Ehrenfest time, about $\log_2\log_2 N$ steps are resolved, four at our largest sizes. Near $w_c$ the 16-cycle perturbs the 8-multiplet through a return path that classically opens only at $w_c$. Cutting a few sites of this path removes the perturbation. candidates.title: An all-orders proof of gradient flow for multiscalar $φ^4$ theory in four dimensions
candidates.comment: 52 pages, 2 figures. Companion paper on d=4-epsilon and other critical dimensions to appear
candidates.abstract: We prove that the renormalisation group flow of multiscalar $φ^4$ theory in four dimensions is a gradient flow to all orders in perturbation theory. The proof uses the Weyl consistency conditions of Osborn and Jack, and it assumes two properties of perturbation theory: that the generating functional with local couplings is finite (also assumed by Osborn and Jack), and that the known expansion of massive Feynman integrals at large momenta holds with a bound on its remainder at each momentum. The consistency conditions give a gradient formula in which the tensor that multiplies the beta function is allowed to have an antisymmetric part, determined by coefficients of the Weyl anomaly. We derive a Ward identity for the two-point function of the marginal operators at constant couplings away from fixed points, with sources for the currents of field rotations and for the mass operator. It re-expresses one of the anti-symmetric contributions in terms of two-point functions and the first moment of the three-point function. candidates.title: Polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling by Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum in bulk WS2 metasurfaces
candidates.abstract: High-refractive-index dielectric metasurfaces supporting optical modes are ideal candidates for achieving strong coupling with transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) materials. However, optical illumination with a specific polarization is always required to estimate the maximal coupling strength in such coupled systems due to the polarization-dependent optical modes. Here, we propose a self-hybridized strong coupling between Brillouin zone folding induced quasi-bound states in the continuum (BZF-QBICs) mode and A excitons in the same bulk WS2 metasurface. By changing the thickness of the bulk WS2 metasurfaces, a typical anticrossing behavior with Rabi splitting of 165.9 meV is observed. Such Rabi splitting is unchanged when changing the polarization of the incident light from linearly to circularly polarizations, demonstrating the polarization-independent self-hybridized strong coupling. This work provides a novel method for realizing robust polarization-independent polaritons in bulk TMDCs metasurface and offers new insights for expanding the applications of polaritonic devices with arbitrary polarizations.

candidates.title: Analysis of Geometric Eigenmode Splitting in Planar Microwave Resonators
candidates.abstract: A traditional challenge in planar microwave resonator design is to find geometric mechanisms that can control individual resonant frequencies - or tune coupling between specific eigenmodes - without affecting other system parameters, such as the center frequency. Achieving this capability can be transformative for the design of microwave sensors, filters, antennas and resonant networks. Starting from first principles, we outline the development of an analytical method that guides practical design by suggesting specific perturbation shapes capable of achieving resonant mode-splitting while keeping the center frequency nearly stationary. This approach opens the door to novel designs that were previously difficult to discover or optimize. Independent numerical simulations and measurements of stripline resonators validate the effectiveness of this approach. The demonstrated tuning effect shows that the first-order estimate suggested by the theory persists in practice over a relatively wide splitting bandwidth (exceeding 54% of center frequency), increasing the utility of the proposed method.

candidates.title: Extensive-Rank Matrix Denoising Under i.i.d. Non-Gaussian Noise
candidates.abstract: We study extensive-rank matrix denoising for rotationally invariant signals corrupted by i.i.d. non-Gaussian noise. To exploit both the signal spectrum and the entrywise noise prior, we consider an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) algorithm that alternates between a rotationally invariant spectral estimator and an entrywise denoiser. At each OAMP iteration, we conjecture a high-dimensional Gaussian equivalence property: the entrywise module admits an effective additive scalar Gaussian channel, whereas the spectral module behaves as if corrupted by i.i.d. Gaussian noise of matching variance. Under this conjecture, we formulate a state evolution (SE) recursion for the effective noise variances of both modules. Numerical simulations confirm that the SE predictions closely track the empirical mean-square errors. For robust principal component analysis (PCA), we apply this OAMP algorithm and characterize its recovery phase diagram via SE. Numerical results show that OAMP achieves a larger recovery region than several existing methods.

candidates.title: An informational interpretation of the reverse nonequilibrium molecular dynamics
candidates.abstract: Reverse nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (RNEMD) is an efficient simulation method for determining transport coefficients. In this method, a flux is imposed by a seemingly artificial nonlocal exchange operation and the corresponding thermodynamic gradient is induced as a result, apparently reversing the usual force-flux causality. Although this method is well studied as a simulation technique, developing an information-thermodynamic interpretation of its Maxwell-demon-type operation and the associated apparent reversal of force-flux causality would provide a solid physical foundation for algorithms of this type. Here, we develop an information-reservoir interpretation for a representative RNEMD scheme for determining self-diffusivity. We show that the statistical bias of the information reservoir defines an information affinity that sustains a concentration gradient and a diffusive flux in the steady state. We further derive the linear transport coefficient corresponding to the information affinity in the linear response regime. candidates.title: DeepDOSReasoner: Physics-Grounded Reasoning for Density-of-States Prediction and Materials Discovery
candidates.comment: Code and data are available on the project page: https://yingheng-wang.com/DeepDOSReasoner/
candidates.abstract: Predicting a material's behavior from its atomic structure is a longstanding goal of the physical sciences. The electronic and phonon densities of states (eDOS and phDOS) govern key electronic, optical, vibrational, and thermodynamic properties, yet their calculation using density functional theory (DFT) is costly: about 60% of Materials Project entries lack eDOS and over 80% lack phDOS. Existing crystal-to-spectrum models rely on pooled structural representations and pointwise regression, which blur spectral features and violate total-state conservation. Here we introduce DeepDOSReasoner, a physics-grounded framework that decodes spectra through atom-to-energy source attention and refines the normalized DOS through learned continuity-equation transport, enforcing nonnegativity and total-state conservation by construction. DeepDOSReasoner achieves the highest prediction accuracy across all evaluated metrics for both eDOS and phDOS, recovers element-resolved contributions without supervision, and most reliably identifies rare valence-band (VB) gaps. candidates.title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
candidates.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to SciPost Physics. Code: https://github.com/AnaamMustafa/Pu241-Neutrino-Mass-Supplement
candidates.abstract: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass. Its low nuclear mass leads to substantial recoil energy, limiting measurements with both molecular tritium ($T_2$) and atomic tritium bound to a substrate. With a beta-decay endpoint energy and half-life similar to those of tritium, but a much larger nuclear mass, $^{241}$Pu may offer an interesting alternative. Its principal challenge is background from the beta decay of $^{237}$U. We discuss strategies for suppressing this background and compare the projected neutrino-mass sensitivities of $^{241}$Pu and tritium as a function of the background suppression.

candidates.title: A Camera-Based Single-Volume, Monolithic Compton Camera
candidates.abstract: A Compton camera measures two events in a detector from individual gamma-rays to reconstruct the radiation source. Conventional scintillator-based Compton cameras consist of two separate scintillator volumes or a single segmented scintillator, resulting in drawbacks regarding detector bulkiness and efficiency. Their scintillator readout techniques struggle to resolve two nearby events in one monolithic scintillator. Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras have recently been proposed for measuring scintillation events in various configurations. SPAD array sensors enable high-resolution photon-counting acquisition at high rates that is easily scalable to millions of pixels. Prior work has explored different optics and measurement arrangements as well as demonstrated measurement of single interaction locations. In this work, we extend these capabilities to demonstrate a practical radiation imaging device in the form of a Compton camera consisting of a SPAD camera and one compact, monolithic scintillator. Our Compton camera prototype successfully reconstructs a gamma-ray source over multiple locations that span a 4$π$ steradian field of view. Our approach is able to resolve two si

candidates.title: Interface invariants of rhombohedral graphene with layer-dependent potentials and couplings
candidates.abstract: Domain walls in the perpendicular bias of rhombohedral (ABC-stacked) graphene bind valley-resolved interface modes whose signed number is fixed by a bulk-difference invariant. We determine which values of this invariant are reachable when the layer potentials are arbitrary monotone profiles, as produced by screening, and when the interlayer couplings vary from bond to bond. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. candidates.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
candidates.abstract: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap. We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. candidates.title: Efficient phase-only wavefront shaping at 250 kHz for multimode fiber endomicroscopy
candidates.abstract: Wavefront shaping through multimode fibers (MMFs) enables diffraction-limited fluorescence imaging with hair-thin probes, at a speed and light budget bounded by the wavefront modulator. Existing modulators provide at most two of three key characteristics: high refresh rate, (high) modal dimensionality, and light efficiency. Here, we demonstrate wavefront control through an MMF using a tailored phase-only microelectromechanical modulator that combines all three, with 8,192 elements arranged in a 32 x 256 array, 7-bit phase control, and a 250 kHz full-frame refresh rate. Direct on-axis phase modulation delivers 70+/-5% of the incident light into the modulated field and eliminates both off-axis encoding optical losses and hologram computation. The generated foci at the distal end of the fiber remain isotropic with high fidelity. We use singular-value decomposition analysis of the measured transmission to identify the effective degrees of freedom of our system. By scanning the focus at multiple depths, we demonstrate volumetric fluorescence imaging. These results open a new operating regime for adaptive in vivo multimode-fiber endoscopy.

candidates.title: Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications
candidates.comment: 16 pages, 3 figures. Mathematica notebooks and verification scripts included as ancillary files
candidates.abstract: We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.

candidates.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
candidates.abstract: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.

candidates.title: Observation of nonadiabatic quantum tunneling in a driven correlated insulator
candidates.comment: 9 pages main text, 4 figures, 33 pages supplementary information
candidates.abstract: Many emerging solid-state platforms for Floquet engineering, nonlinear transport, and high harmonic generation operate near the Keldysh crossover, where optical fields are sufficiently strong and fast to reshape electronic states on sub-cycle timescales. Despite its importance, the microscopic pathways for photocarrier generation in this regime remain poorly understood, as neither perturbative multiphoton absorption nor adiabatic tunneling provides an adequate description. Here, we perform time-resolved optical spectroscopy on the correlated van der Waals insulator NiPS$_3$ while systematically tuning the drive electric field and frequency over a wide range. In the crossover regime, we observe multiphoton-like resonances that are blue-shifted by ponderomotive effects within an otherwise tunneling-dominated absorption channel - a clear spectroscopic signature of adiabaticity breakdown. Hubbard-model simulations based on a time-dependent Gaussian variational approach qualitatively reproduce these features. candidates.title: Handed Ultrafast Dynamics in Chiral Cyanine Nanotubes
candidates.abstract: We detect helicity-dependent excited state relaxation in a chiral exciton system. Using L-histidine as a chiral inducer, we prepared unbundled, double-walled J-aggregrate nanotubes of an amphiphilic cyanine dye with a net handedness, which gives a large circular dichroism dissymmetry factor ($g_{abs} = 3.6 \times 10^{-2}$). With two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy and circularly polarized pump pulses, we find that the relaxation rates of longitudinal excitons depend on pump helicity (4.5 $ps^{-1}$ for $\langle \textit{RRXX} \rangle$ vs 6 $ps^{-1}$ for $\langle \textit{LLXX} \rangle$, a difference of about 30%) and is the same in the inner and outer tubes. Transverse excitons show no significant dependence. Chirality and pump helicity therefore bias exciton relaxation on the femtosecond timescale for excitons delocalized along the helical structure.

candidates.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
candidates.abstract: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins. Semiclassical methods can reach these sizes, but their classical treatment of the bath cannot capture the sensor-bath entanglement that generates coherence revivals, especially under the application of refocusing pulses. Here, we resolve this tension. We introduce cluster spin-LSC, a method that clusters the sensor together with a few strongly coupled bath spins, treating them quantum mechanically in an otherwise classical spin bath. We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences. Our method converges systematically to the exact dynamics with cluster size, providing an internal consistency check when no exact benchmarks exist. candidates.title: Data handling, production, and simulation in the Muon g-2 Experiment at Fermilab
candidates.abstract: This paper details the computing strategies of the Muon g-2 Experiment at Fermilab, which measured the muon's anomalous magnetic moment with a precision of 127 ppb by processing over 10 petabytes of detector and simulation data. This paper discusses the computational and operational challenges of data production, data handling, and data analysis of such large datasets. These challenges were overcome by using Fermilab-developed software infrastructure and production tools, making efficient use of resources, and improving the collaboration-developed reconstruction workflow. By overcoming these challenges, the experiment improved the data throughput capacity and reduced the analysis turnaround time by an order of magnitude over the course of its lifetime.

candidates.title: Metastable states are precursors of Turing patterns in Adaptive Networks
candidates.abstract: In networked reaction-diffusion systems, emergence of patterns from a homogeneous equilibrium can be described by Turing instability. Recently, Turing theory has been developed to include adaptive networks where, i.e., link weights change as a function of the states of the nodes. In this work we show that metastable states, defined as long living transient epochs with unique dynamical properties, could be observed in a range of parameters between Turing patterns and absence of any spatial pattern. Stated differently in the metastable regime the system ''switches'' between the homogeneous solution and the Turing pattern, never settling in any of those states, i.e., alternating silent and spiking regimes. By using phase diagrams and recurrence plots, we have numerically shown the existence of metastable states for the Brusselator model. Moreover, the dependence of the emergence of the metastable states on the adaptive control parameter has been characterized. The applicability of methods and ideas proposed in this work go beyond the considered case, they can help us in understanding conditions under which metastable states arise and could thus be informative to predict and control th

candidates.title: Learning free energy across a differentiable temperature range by deep generative modeling
candidates.abstract: Free energy governs the directionality, stability, and temperature sensitivity of physical, chemical, and biological transformations. Conventional free energy calculations, such as thermodynamic integration and free energy perturbation, often have to be performed at individual temperatures and are limited by the high cost of sampling an extensive set of thermodynamic states. Here, we introduce learned temperature-differentiable free energy perturbation (TD-FEP), a deep generative framework that learns a temperature-conditioned, invertible mapping between reference and target systems through data-free, energy-based optimization. TD-FEP thereby unifies one-shot state generation and free energy calculation across a continuous temperature range. We validated TD-FEP across a broad range of applications, including isolated molecules, periodic materials, and chemical reactions.

candidates.title: Minimal Three-Band Model and $d$-Wave Superconductivity in La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_8$
candidates.abstract: Motivated by the recent observation of ambient-pressure superconductivity in Pr- and Y-substituted La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_8$, we combined density-functional theory (DFT), dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), random phase approximation (RPA), and fluctuation exchange approximation (FLEX) methods to study its electronic structure and superconducting pairing symmetry. DFT band analysis indicates that the low-energy states are mainly dominated by three Ni-3$d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals with weak $d$-$p$ hybridization. Multi-orbital DMFT calculations yield an average $d_{x^2-y^2}$ filling of about 0.87, close to the optimal value for infinite-layer nickelates. By comparing the DMFT results of $d_{x^2-y^2}$ only and full Ni-3$d$ models, we find that their electronic properties are almost completely consistent, demonstrating the effectiveness of the simplified $d_{x^2-y^2}$ model. RPA and FLEX calculations based on this model consistently indicate a dominant $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing instability. candidates.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
candidates.abstract: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints, and identify energy--momentum conservation with covariance of the constitutive Lagrangian. The nonrelativistic limit and a relation of entropy-level helicity to split Calabi--Yau geometry are briefly indicated.

candidates.title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
candidates.abstract: Designing low-thrust multi-asteroid rendezvous missions requires the coupled selection of asteroid sequences, encounter epochs, and low-thrust trajectories. Lambert transfers support rapid beam search but do not directly describe thrust-limited transfer capacity or propellant consumption. This paper develops two complementary low-thrust neural approximators. The first directly predicts the continuous maximum admissible initial mass from numerically optimized low-thrust transfers, providing a transfer-capacity estimate for comparison with the current spacecraft mass. The second predicts mass-dependent propellant consumption and propagates spacecraft mass to subsequent legs. With the carefully-designed input features and network structure, the approximators reduce mean absolute errors by 72.2% and 75.5%, respectively, relative to conventional deep neural network baselines. These predictions are incorporated into a Lambert-ranked beam search through resource filtering and recursive mass propagation before final beam selection. The method is evaluated on fixed-visit, maximum-visit, and deployment-collection missions. Across the tested cases, the proposed resource filtering increases th

candidates.title: LayerCake v1.0: a framework for low- to intermediate-order automated models development
candidates.comment: 19 pages, 3 figures, submitted to Geoscientific Model Development (GMD)
candidates.abstract: A new model development framework called LayerCake is presented. It is written in the Python language and relies on the Sympy symbolic computation package to compute the Galerkin projection of two-dimensional spatially extended geophysical models. These projections provide their time evolution operator in the spectral space on a restricted set of modes. The resulting tendencies of the models can be evaluated either numerically (for time integration) or symbolically (for parameters sensitivity analysis and bifurcation analysis). We provide several simple examples of geophysical models to showcase the capabilities of the framework, and we hint at how more complex systems can be designed.

candidates.title: An equivariant classical density functional for ionic fluids at complex interfaces
candidates.abstract: Predicting the combined effects of ionic packing and long-range electrostatics at complex interfaces is technologically important, but remains challenging without atomistic simulations. Here we present a machine-learned classical density functional for ionic fluids that combines a symmetry-adapted neural free energy for short-range correlations with explicit long-range electrostatics. Trained on three-dimensional equilibrium densities and bulk correlations of the full-Coulomb restricted primitive model, a single functional transfers to charge-patterned particles and atomically structured electrodes. Around anisotropic charged solutes, it reproduces the ionic structure and mean forces from molecular dynamics, including reversals of the bare electrostatic force. At metal electrodes, self-consistent coupling to metal atoms captures the redistribution of ionic and electrode charge and the loading-dependent capacitance enhancement produced by steps and bumps. Combined with mobilities determined independently from bulk molecular dynamics, the same functional describes the main features of charging dynamics and resolves geometry-dependent spatial relaxation. This framework can be extended

candidates.title: Accelerating wave-scattering simulations with learned search directions
candidates.abstract: Wave-scattering simulation requires solving a dense boundary-element system for every frequency, incidence and design. Krylov solvers build each search space from scratch, and it grows with problem size. Here we present BEMFormer, a solver that learns to generate search directions across systems of one integral equation and supplies geometry-specific directions through a coarse-grid correction. BEMFormer generalizes to unseen geometries, meshes and excitations, and to acoustic scattering after fine-tuning on eight geometries. It reproduces the measured radar cross-sections of benchmark targets. On a quadcopter with 1.04 million unknowns, 38 times the largest training problem, BEMFormer solves each system 30 times faster than a preconditioned Krylov solver. Both reach a radar cross-section deviation of about 1 dB, comparable to the difference between independent measurements and acceptable for engineering applications. These results show that solving million-unknown scattering problems in minutes is possible when the search space is learned rather than built from scratch.

candidates.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
candidates.abstract: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.

candidates.title: Distinguishing photothermal and photoelectrokinetic contributions to flow in light-activated microchannel architectures
candidates.comment: 31 pages, 5 figures. Main text only; Supplementary Information will be provided in a later version
candidates.abstract: Light-driven flows near Janus surfaces could power microfluidic devices without external hardware. These flows are often attributed to photoinduced electro- or diffusio-osmosis, but illumination also heats the surface, potentially driving natural convection. Here, we map flow and temperature around a UVA-illuminated TiO$_2$-Au Janus membrane using depth-resolved particle tracking and infrared thermometry. Recirculating rolls form on both sides, with no measurable net flow across the membrane. Their cubic, reversing velocity profile identifies horizontal (Hadley) convection, driven by a lateral temperature gradient as the gold film absorbs light. The measured profile agrees with wall-corrected Hadley theory using one fitted parameter. Adding 100 mM NaCl to suppress electrokinetic flows leaves the profile unchanged, indicating that convection dominates. Simulations show that convection falls below 1 $μ$m/s in thin channels, where surface-driven osmotic flows could dominate. Thus, device geometry and surface chemistry determine which mechanism governs light-driven microfluidic flows.

candidates.title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
candidates.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 1 table; submitted to ApJ
candidates.abstract: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datas

candidates.title: Expressive Shallow Networks for Physics-Informed Learning: Why Curvature-Aware Optimization and FP64 Are Not Enough
candidates.comment: Submitted to the Journal of Computational Physics
candidates.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often struggle with high-frequency and high-order partial differential equations (PDEs) due to optimization stiffness and spectral bias, despite possessing sufficient approximation capacity. Existing remedies, including modified feature representations, domain decomposition, higher floating-point precision, and curvature-aware optimizers, can improve convergence but largely act as workarounds for optimization difficulties arising from deep architectures rather than addressing their underlying source. We investigate Physics-Informed Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (PI-SUPNs), which replace deep nonlinear compositions with learnable polynomial expansions, retaining high approximation capacity within a shallow computational graph. On a high-frequency Helmholtz benchmark, PI-SUPNs are the only architecture to successfully recover the solution, while all competing models fail even under FP64 precision and curvature-aware optimization. However, experiments on higher vibrational modes of a fourth-order Euler-Bernoulli beam reveal that architectural improvements alone are insufficient: accurate solutions require the combination of PI-SUPNs, FP

candidates.title: Real-time event-level zero-shot learning at 150 ns: towards a foundation model for particle physics experiment triggering
candidates.comment: 29 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to SciPost Physics
candidates.abstract: The hardware-based Level-1 triggers of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments select collisions with algorithms designed for one signature each, acting on a coarse, low-latency view of every event. We present a learned event embedding for several trigger tasks and evaluate its transfer to processes absent from training. Using paired offline and Level-1 views of the same simulated collisions, we train an offline transformer with a supervised metric loss and distil it, event by event, into a quantised Level-1 transformer whose bit widths are learned under a fixed resource budget. Trained on 25 Standard Model processes, the embedding places 28 held-out processes next to their physical relatives. A nearest-neighbour selection against background collisions, which never enter encoder training, rejects 99% of them. It retains a median of 90% of seen and 96% of unseen Standard Model events and 88% of a set of 52 beyond-the-Standard-Model benchmark samples, the best-performing score across the three groups among the baselines evaluated on the same events. candidates.title: Where does a molecule begin? Threshold masses of three-particle Coulomb systems and a predictive theory of their Born-Oppenheimer offsets
candidates.comment: ESI attached at the end of the paper
candidates.abstract: The Born-Oppenheimer (BO) approximation serves as the foundational framework for the contemporary concept of molecular structure, which is central to chemistry and the molecular sciences. Its principal assumption is the treatment of nuclei as infinitely heavy particles. In this work, we test the boundaries of the BO approximation by examining systems with variable nuclear masses to investigate the emergence of molecular structure. We examine the three-particle family {X^+,X^+,e^-} as a function of the mass ratio M = m_X/m_e, using deterministic variational calculations and the exact BO approximation. We accurately compute the threshold masses of all 23 excited levels bound below M = 100 with certified upper bounds. The BO approximation places every one of them too late by a nearly constant amount, 1.2 to 1.6 (0.23 to 0.54 with the adiabatic correction). We explain this constancy with a parameter-free theory, and test it with predictions frozen before the exact calculations: 18 of 18 symmetric levels pass (typical miss 0.003). candidates.title: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
candidates.abstract: We study the cutoff Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie--King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman--Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy--Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff system by the linear equation of state $P=ρc^2/\sqrt3$ in the physical wedge $0<y\leq3x$. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors--Stańczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is $2Gm(r)/(rc^2)<0.6879212521$. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to $0.6734385929$. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.

candidates.title: CHARMS250V1: A Cryogenic Front-End ASIC for Low-Noise Readout of Charge or Light Signals in Noble Liquid Detectors
candidates.abstract: This work presents the design and measurement results of CHARMS250V1, a next-generation cryogenic front-end application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) developed using a 65 nm CMOS process. It is designed for low-noise readout of charge or light signals generated in noble liquid detectors. CHARMS250V1 is a single channel prototype whose design in the future will be integrated within a 16-channel ASIC. It comprises pre-amplification and pulse shaping stages that provide programmable charge gain between 4.3 mV/fC and 25 mV/fC, peaking time programmable between 250 ns and 2 us, and programmable baseline of either 200 mV or 900 mV for processing of unipolar and bipolar signals, respectively.

candidates.title: Observation of collective flatbands in hybrid Mie-grating THz metasurfaces
candidates.comment: 12 pages of main text with 5 figures; 20 pages of Supporting Information with 12 supplementary figures. This work elucidates the microscopic origins of collective photonic band structures through multipolar interactions within the Mie-tronics framework
candidates.abstract: We propose a novel type of functional metasurfaces created by a hybridization of Mie resonators with high-index optical gratings. We demonstrate that such hybrid metasurfaces possess flatbands characterized by zero group velocity and strong energy localization. We experimentally observe the flatbands in free-standing terahertz (THz) metasurfaces, where dielectric interconnections between Mie resonators, forming the grating, mediate multipolar hybridization and provide a geometric control over collective resonances. Our THz near-field measurements with a dipole excitation uncover long-lived coherent oscillations associated with the quasi-flat magnetic-dipolar resonant modes, while a spatial mapping resolves the resonant electromagnetic response across the dielectric interconnections. We vary the grating width continuously to tune the hybrid magnetic-dipolar resonances and substantially enhance the quality factor (Q factor), while preserving the quasi-!atband dispersion. candidates.title: Nonequilibrium fluctuations could explain the hot mitochondria paradox
candidates.comment: 4 pages, 2 figures. Any comments are very welcome!
candidates.abstract: Several different experiments have found apparent temperature differences of up to 10 K between the interior of mitochondria and the rest of the cellular environment. The physics of heat conduction, however, precludes the steady-state existence of a temperature difference greater than the microkelvin scale within the cell, absent a far greater energy budget. Nearly a decade after the first reported measurement, this apparent paradox remains unexplained. Here, we propose an explanation which allows the elevated temperature measurements to coexist with the theoretical impossibility of a true 10 K steady-state temperature difference. We suggest that nonequilibrium fluctuations within the cellular environment, combined with molecular temperature probes sensitive to specific ranges of frequencies, can lead to apparent 10 K temperature differences with a biologically attainable power budget.

candidates.title: State-selective dynamical freezing in driven Rydberg atom chains
candidates.abstract: Dynamical freezing, the near-complete suppression of dynamics at special drive frequencies, offers a route to mitigating Floquet heating in periodically driven quantum systems. In interacting systems, however, the energy cost of each transition depends on the many-body configuration, so that the freezing condition itself becomes state dependent. We study this dependence in periodically driven Rydberg atom chains under single- and bi-frequency driving. Using Floquet perturbation theory, we show that each spin flip is characterised by a single interference amplitude set by its local interaction shift, and that a state freezes only where the amplitudes of all its available flips vanish simultaneously. This picture accounts quantitatively for the shift and proliferation of freezing frequencies with interatomic spacing and for the response of entire families of initial states, which are sorted by a single local motif. Freezing is strong only within a window of spacings bounded by interaction tails on one side and nearest-neighbour excitation facilitation on the other, outside of which the advantage of bi-frequency driving is lost. candidates.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
candidates.abstract: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

candidates.title: The index from a super-point
candidates.abstract: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of filtered graded rings that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories whose Schur sector contains fermionic generators. The rings are then $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded-commutative, and the index is reproduced by the Hilbert series of a generalized arc space, whose defining ideal may contain relations among the generators and their derivatives. We study the free $\mathcal{N}=2$ vector multiplet, $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills with gauge algebras $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(3)$, the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, and the $\widehat{E}_6(SU(2))$ SCFT. For the rank-one $\mathcal{N}=3$ SCFTs, the ideal is the sum of the Jacobian ideals of a single superpotential and of its two supersymmetry variations. For $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills, the ideal is similarly the sum of the Jacobian ideals of the components of a single $\mathcal{N}=4$ superfield, which is a singlet of the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ flavor symmetry for gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and a triplet for $\mathfrak{su}(3)$. candidates.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
candidates.abstract: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. candidates.title: CLFF: Automated Framework for Concurrent Learning Force Fields and Material Property Calculations
candidates.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer an efficient paradigm for large-scale atomistic simulations with near first-principles accuracy. However, developing and deploying these potentials often involves intricate procedures that require substantial manual effort and domain expertise. In this work, we present CLFF, an open-source Python framework designed to automate concurrent learning workflows for MLIPs. CLFF integrates model training, MLIP-driven sampling, uncertainty-based candidate selection, quantum-mechanical labeling, and dataset augmentation into a unified workflow. The framework currently supports several modern graph-based MLIP architectures and is compatible with widely used computational chemistry and materials science tools. A distinguishing feature of CLFF is its ability to asynchronously distribute computational tasks across multiple heterogeneous remote computing resources, enabling users to aggregate fragmented hardware infrastructure within a single controllable workflow. In addition to concurrent learning, CLFF provides automated workflows for initial data generation and material property calculations, including phonon dispersion and potential ener

candidates.title: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
candidates.abstract: We formulate the dissipation due to sound-wave emission from a Keplerian binary embedded in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background at rest in the binary center-of-mass frame within linear perturbation theory. Rather than starting from the local wake force, we treat the binary as a localized periodic mass source and compute the sound-wave fluxes carried away by the medium. The time-averaged energy, linear-momentum, and angular-momentum fluxes are obtained from Noether currents of the fluid perturbations. For a classical inviscid barotropic Newtonian fluid, retaining the self-gravity of density perturbations while adopting the Jeans prescription, we derive explicit flux formulas for circular and eccentric binaries with arbitrary mass ratio. This formulation also clarifies the ultraviolet behavior of point sources: in a nondispersive fluid, the harmonic sum becomes cutoff-sensitive precisely when at least one component becomes supersonic. We examine explicitly how finite source size removes this divergence using a uniform-sphere model and relate the resulting regularization to a corresponding effective harmonic cutoff. candidates.title: Identifying Distant and Highly Reddened Star Clusters: 486 Open Clusters and Candidates in the Dusty Galactic Disk
candidates.comment: The 486 new cluster data can be downloaded from https://zenodo.org/records/24431850
candidates.abstract: The Gaia mission has transformed the census of Galactic star clusters. Most discoveries were based on Gaia DR2 and EDR3, and the rate of new large cluster catalogues has declined since 2023. The distant and dusty part of the disk is still poorly sampled because optical data are strongly affected by extinction. We search for star clusters in the Galactic disk using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, together with 2MASS near-infrared photometry. We scan trial cluster centers in Galactic position, proper motion, and parallax space, assign a Bayesian membership probability to each star, construct a relative density map, and use DBSCAN solely to separate neighboring peaks. We identify 486 clusters and candidates with astrometric quality comparable to that of previously reported clusters. Of these, 450 have no literature counterpart, while 36 are known clusters that were not recovered in earlier Gaia cluster searches. The median distance is 6.9 kpc, and 39% of the objects lie beyond 8 kpc. The median extinction is Av = 5.10 mag, and 16% of the objects have Av > 8mag. The new objects fill a sparsely sampled region of the distance--extinction plane. Their distribution reveals the north--s

candidates.title: Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers
candidates.comment: 177 pages, 4 figures, 13 tables. Archive and Lean sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24254845
candidates.abstract: Below a threshold noise rate, error correction lets larger quantum memories store a qubit for longer, without limit. Can the noise rate alone tell us whether a given noisy circuit does this? We construct fixed local circuits for which no algorithm can, already in one dimension under single-qubit noise. Each circuit is translation-invariant and time-periodic, with depolarizing noise on every wire after every layer, including all classical control. A computable list of disjoint rate intervals is indexed by the inputs $n$ of a universal Turing machine; local noise statistics select the input that the circuit simulates, and halting triggers erasure. If the machine runs forever on $n$, a qubit is stored throughout the $n$-th interval at entanglement fidelity at least $15/16$ for a time that grows without bound with size: linearly on rings, exponentially in six dimensions. The encoding and decoding maps are noiseless and global; they depend on $n$, the system size and, for decoding, the time, but not on the rate. candidates.title: Single-Shot Single-Stage Stellarators
candidates.abstract: In stellarator design, the plasma and the coils are so geometrically complex that they are usually designed separately, so that a high-performance plasma may be impossible to reproduce with coils that can actually be manufactured and assembled. We present a new method to close this gap. In this framework, the plasma shape is optimized while, for every candidate shape, near-optimal coils that satisfy hard engineering limits are found. Without any manually-tuned weights, the method steers the plasma towards shapes that real coils can produce. Moreover, we demonstrate the first single-shot optimization runs starting from tokamak ``cold-starts''. Starting from a boundary derived from W7-X, we design a quasi-isodynamic stellarator with reactor-relevant stability properties. candidates.title: Uniguided and unicoupled resonances in an asymmetric acoustic metasurface
candidates.abstract: We theoretically study an acoustic metasurface that exhibits ultimate asymmetry in absorption under oblique incidence. This behavior arises from a counter-propagating pair of uniguided (UGR) and unicoupled (UCR) resonances. The UGR radiates to only one side, while the UCR radiates to both sides but can be excited from only one. In the lossless regime, the transmission phase winds by $2π$ across both UCR and UGR while the transmittance remains flat at any prescribed nonzero level. Thermoviscous losses introduce resonant intensity modulation and enable critical coupling, yielding perfect sound absorption exclusively for incidence through the channel that excites the UCR. Therefore, asymmetric metasurfaces with UCR and UGR offer a route to full phase control and perfect sound absorption.

candidates.title: Fractal dimension of velocity-driven mixing: Reanalysis of Cao et al. (Phys. Rev. A 45, 3841 (1992)) and the universality of the Marstrand co-dimension rule
candidates.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures, draft to be published
candidates.abstract: Cao et al. [Phys. Rev. candidates.abstract: Accurate modelling of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) coils requires coil-specific geometric and electrical parameters. Yet detailed manufacturer models are rarely available, and internals may be widely available to companies in the field but not to researchers. The development of new coils should ideally build on all existing prior art. This work presents a technology benchmark and modelling-ready dataset for seventeen widely used commercial TMS coils across multiple manufacturers and geometries. Complementary electrical measurements provide spectral impedance (series resistance and inductance) scans from 20 Hz to 200 kHz, together with dc resistance. candidates.title: Path Integrals on Functional Lattices
candidates.abstract: Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a Galerkin argument. candidates.title: Optical Motion Sensing for Piezoelectric-Resonator-Based Power Converters
candidates.abstract: Piezoelectric components present a promising alternative to conventional magnetics for miniaturized, high-frequency power converters. While high-Q piezoelectric resonators have demonstrated high efficiencies and large power densities in prototype high-frequency dc-dc converters, their optimal operating conditions are sensitive to temperature fluctuations and load variations. Therefore, robust closed-loop control is essential for practical deployment. Electrical approaches for sensing motional current may compromise the electrical isolation and electromagnetic interference (EMI) immunity inherently provided by the mechanical nature of these resonators. The proposed approach uses optical interference to monitor the mechanical displacement in real time. candidates.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
candidates.abstract: A physician checks the clinical electrocardiogram against other observations. A wearable monitor has no physician. This paper shows that a mechanical sensor worn beside the electrocardiogram can take over that check, and that the right added sensors lower false alarms further. Shifting the mechanical signal in time removed the benefit. A detection criterion scores an added sensor by the part of its response that the sensors in place cannot predict. With four sensors, this score ranked the sets as their measured false-alarm rates did. With the two sensors it selected, 6.2 percent of the artifacts passed while 95 percent of true beats were kept, half the rate of the best single sensor. candidates.abstract: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)ρ(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(χ)\rangle =\langle ρ(χ)\rangle \langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $χ$ is the scale of the system under study and it can describe cosmological or galactic scales and $σ_{DM}$ is the characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter at the relevant scales. This results to the entropy function behaving universally as $K(χ)=\langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$. candidates.abstract: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

candidates.title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
candidates.abstract: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.

candidates.title: On locked states for damped driven Jaynes--Cummings equations
candidates.abstract: We consider damped driven version of the Jaynes-Cummings equation which describes quantised one-mode Maxwell field coupled to a two-level molecule. The pumping and dissipation operator are polynomial in the creation and annihilation operators. The structure of the dissipation operator corresponds to the theory of completely positive trace preserving operators due to Lindblad, Kossakowski and others. We construct examples of {\it locked states} which are stationary states of the corresponding averaged dynamics in the interaction picture. The states are nonnegative Hermitian density operators with finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The calculations rely on the recurrence equation for diagonal entries.

candidates.title: Q-TRACE: Physics-based zero-day attack detection for decoy-state quantum key distribution
candidates.comment: 33 pages, 11 figures, 14 tables. Code, raw hardware data and all results are available at https://github.com/Sumitchongder/Q-TRACE
candidates.abstract: Practical quantum key distribution (QKD) is secure only while its devices match the assumptions of the security proof, and implementation attacks exploit mismatches while keeping the quantum bit error rate (QBER) low. We formulate attack detection in decoy-state BB84 as a sequential test against the honest-device manifold, the set of receiver statistics an attack-free link can produce under arbitrary channel loss. The resulting monitor, Q-TRACE (Quantum Telemetry Residuals Against Calibrated Expectations), calibrates a physical model of each link on commissioning data, profiles out the transmittance, and combines omnibus residual, physics score and setting-allocation tests with drift-robust references; no attack data are used. The formulation also yields a detectability exponent D* that lower-bounds the delay of any telemetry monitor and vanishes for a Trojan-horse probe with filtered back-reflection. candidates.title: Tuning of superconducting and physical properties of Mo$_{1-x}$Si$_x$ thin films for Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detector Applications
candidates.abstract: We investigate the normal-state electrical properties of ultrathin amorphous Mo$_{1-x}$Si$_x$ films deposited by DC magnetron co-sputtering over a broad range of compositions and thicknesses. Films with Si contents of $x = 0.14$ to $0.5$ were deposited on Si/SiO$_2$ and Si/Si$_3$N$_4$ substrates (monocrystalline Si with SiO$_2$ and S$_3$N$_4$ buffer layers respectfully); X-ray diffraction confirms an amorphous structure across the full composition range, while X-ray reflectometry is used to verify film thicknesses. The room-temperature sheet resistance ranges from 110 to 1990 $Ω/\square$, corresponding to resistivities of 125-478 $μΩ\cdot$cm. The sheet resistance generally increases with increasing Si content and decreasing film thickness, although the coupled variation of composition and thickness limits the quantitative separation of these effects. Additional measurements on thicker reference films show superconducting transition temperatures between 5.2 and 7.7 K, with $T_c$ decreasing monotonically at higher Si contents. candidates.title: An Implicit Discrete Adjoint Unified Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Sensitivity Analysis and Shape Optimization in Multiscale Gas Flows
candidates.abstract: Accurate and efficient gradient-based sensitivity evaluation remains challenging for performance optimization in multiscale flows with complex geometries. To address this challenge, this work develops a matrix-free discrete adjoint method for the steady implicit unified gas-kinetic scheme (UGKS) through the exact linearization and transposition of its converged fixed-point operator. The method employs a hybrid differentiation strategy that combines local automatic differentiation (AD) of complex nonlinear kinetic kernels with analytically derived tangent and transpose operators for the coupled macroscopic--microscopic implicit updates and mass-conservation projection. This formulation ensures exact discrete consistency across both flow and geometric dependencies while avoiding global Jacobian assembly and the memory overhead of end-to-end reverse-mode AD. Verification tests across continuum, transitional, and free-molecular regimes confirm machine-precision stepwise duality with the corresponding tangent-linear solver and close agreement with central finite differences. candidates.title: DIPS-OjOS I: Project Design and Science Validation
candidates.comment: 18 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in PASP. This is the version originally submitted to the journal, before peer review
candidates.abstract: Automated pipelines and machine-learning algorithms are efficient at detecting standard planetary transits, but can miss subtle, non-periodic morphological anomalies. We present the pilot phase of DIPS-OjOS (Detecting Irregular Photometric Signals - OjímetrO Survey), a professional-amateur collaboration designed to develop and validate a scalable workflow for identifying irregular photometric signals in exoplanet transit light curves through trained visual inspection. The project targets starspot-crossing events, stellar flares, circumplanetary structures, exomoon-like signatures, and transit-duration or timing anomalies overlooked by automated searches. We built the infrastructure required for a controlled visual-inspection experiment: simulated control light curves, preparation and detrending of real short-cadence Kepler data, a transit-modeling pipeline that computes an optimized average transit profile for each light curve, and a web-based classification platform. The real sample was deliberately restricted to 51 well-characterized Kepler systems. Collaborators inspected 917 transit events: 555 real transits and 362 simulated controls. candidates.title: Long-time dynamics of open quantum systems: mathematical and physical aspects
candidates.abstract: Quantum channels provide the mathematical framework for describing the evolution of open quantum systems, i.e., quantum systems interacting with an environment. This review focuses on the long-time or asymptotic dynamics of open quantum systems, a topic of growing interest due to its relevance for quantum information theory and noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. We present a comprehensive analysis of homogeneous evolutions in both discrete and continuous time, treating the dynamics in full generality within the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures. By systematically studying the spectral properties of quantum channels, we present general structure theorems that characterize asymptotic behaviour, illustrated through several paradigmatic examples. We further discuss how the asymptotic dynamics can be exploited for dissipative state engineering, the identification of decoherence-free subspaces, the design of quantum error-correction schemes, and the evaluation of the asymptotic capacities of quantum channels.

candidates.title: Charge-fluctuation hot lines and superconductivity in Ba$_{1-x}$K$_x$BiO$_3$
candidates.abstract: The origin of superconductivity near 30~K in Ba$_{0.6}$K$_{0.4}$BiO$_3$ has remained a long-standing puzzle. Tunneling experiments give an electron--boson coupling $λ\approx 0.7$--1.2, whereas density-functional calculations give $λ\approx 0.3$, concentrated in the breathing mode near 50--70~meV. We propose that the missing coupling of about 0.7 comes from dynamical charge fluctuations at Q=(pi,pi,pi)/a, the ordering vector of the charge-disproportionated parent compound, and introduce an overdamped boson model to describe them. Using a tight-binding fit to the conduction band found from density-functional calculations at $x=0.4$, we show that such a boson scatters electrons strongly only on hot lines of the Fermi surface, small loops around the $\langle 111\rangle$ directions where k and k+Q are both at the Fermi level. We derive closed-form self-energies, quasiparticle residues and band reconstructions, including shadow bands and hot-line pseudogaps for long-range correlations, and show that a sum rule fixes the Fermi-surface-averaged coupling independently of the boson frequency and correlation length.
