candidates.title: Tipping cascades may lock the Earth system on a pathway towards a melthouse
candidates.abstract: The potential for the Earth system to transition irreversibly into a hothouse Earth has attracted considerable scientific and media attention but remains insufficiently explored in modeling studies. Using a reduced-complexity Earth system model that includes a dynamic carbon cycle and interacting tipping elements, we find no planetary threshold beyond which the Earth system irreversibly shifts into a hothouse state. Instead, tipping cascades can drive the system towards an irreversible melthouse state with over 10 m of sea-level rise. Such cascades may occur even under low-emission scenarios, preventing long-term stabilization of sea level at intermediate values. Our results overall highlight the substantial risk of a melthouse rather than a hothouse Earth, and call for drastic emission reductions to avert dramatic impacts on coastal cities and communities.

candidates.abstract: We present a new method, and its implementation, for constructing orthogonal colour bases and computing colour factors for any process with quarks, antiquarks and gluons, and use it to compute one-loop soft-gluon evolution exactly in full colour, keeping all colour interference. Each basis vector is labelled, independently of $N_c$, by the sequence of colour representations that appear when the partons are coupled one at a time. We derive a closed formula for the norms of the basis vectors, and colour operators act only on the part of a label between the partons involved, through small tables. Basis vectors can therefore be generated and used one at a time, without listing the complete basis: norms and matrix elements of single basis vectors are obtained for $10^4$ gluons in seconds. The same locality lets the soft anomalous dimension act on colour states without being stored. This allows optimised implementations on CPUs and GPUs, with which we evolve colour states exactly for up to fourteen gluons on a single GPU and for fifteen gluons, a colour space of $827\,888\,726$ dimensions, on a single compute node. candidates.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures, plus Supplemental Material (18 pages, 2 figures)
candidates.abstract: A spin flip in the Kitaev honeycomb model changes the flux background and therefore the Hamiltonian seen by the matter fermions. Can a one-particle approximation with the correct total spin intensity nevertheless misestimate the depth of a depression in the local spin spectrum? We test this question in a frozen, flux-disordered ensemble by retaining the actual one-particle transition energies and relative spectral weights after the spin flip, then rescaling those weights to match the full intensity. We measure the depression by subtracting the central intensity from the average at two flanking frequencies. For spin-created states with odd final quasiparticle number and nonzero one-particle weight, restoring multiparticle weight shallows the depression on 24 sites and deepens it on both 1,536-site shapes and the 3,456- and 6,144-site tori, as judged by the median paired correction at each of two energy resolutions. candidates.comment: 13 pages, 1 table. 5 pages of main text and 8 pages of appendices
candidates.abstract: Semiclassical gravity is sourced by the expectation value of the stress tensor, and it is reliable only if the fluctuations around this value are small. In two dimensions, conformal symmetry captures the essential physics of Hawking radiation in its s-wave sector and determines the mean value exactly, for any background and any quantum state. We show that it also determines the local fluctuations of the null components $T_{\pm\pm}$. The square of the stress tensor is defined by the operator product expansion, up to a multiple $α$ of $\partial_\pm^2T_{\pm\pm}$ that labels point-splitting prescriptions. Its transformation law under the conformal map to locally inertial coordinates gives the variance in closed form. The relative fluctuation scales as $1/c$, with $c$ the central charge. For the Schwarzschild black hole it is $22/5c$ for the Hawking flux at infinity, that of flat-space thermal radiation. At the horizon it is $-44α/3c$ for the outgoing flux and $(238+720α)/5c$ for the ingoing flux that drives the backreaction. Both reduce to $22/5c$ for $α=-3/10$, which corresponds to the Möbius-covariant prescription. For large $c$ these results support the semiclassical approximation.

candidates.title: The Schwarzschild Ringdown Time Prescription on Critical Kerr Plunges
candidates.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, including Supplemental Material
candidates.abstract: For a Schwarzschild plunge, constant-amplitude quasinormal-mode convergence has been tied to the source's advanced time at $r=0$, lying $9.435M$ after the $(2,2)$ strain peak. On real prograde critical Kerr plunges, $P(r_-)<0$ forces the ingoing time $v$ to diverge logarithmically at the inner horizon while $u_K$ stays finite. Matching $v$ to $-u_K$ at the unique interior zero $P(r_0)=0$ yields a parameter-free onset hierarchy $(u_{\rm H},u_{r_0},u_{\rm C})$ that recovers $9.435M$ as $a\to 0$ and predicts two-stage residual decay and frequency locking at $(6.85M,11.35M,13.35M)$ on an $a/M=0.9$ eccentric plunge.

candidates.abstract: We study scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac perturbations of an asymptotically flat black hole in parity-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity. candidates.title: Compact and Long-Term Stable Polarization Entangled Photon-Pair Source
candidates.abstract: We present a robust, compact polarization-entangled photon-pair source based on bulk optics that achieves long-term stability, a spectral pair generation rate of $4.24 \times 10^6$ pairs s$^{-1}$ mW$^{-1}$ nm$^{-1}$ constant for pump powers up to 700 mW, an intrinsic heralding efficiency of 59.8% , and a polarization contrast visibility of 99.6%. It operates at telecom wavelengths in C-band with a typical type-0 SPDC spectral output of 70 nm width. We demonstrate its integration into a deployed entanglement-based QKD system that bridges the gap between laboratory prototypes and practical quantum communication hardware.

candidates.comment: Main article: 28 pages and 11 figures. Appendix: 12 pages and 7 figures
candidates.abstract: Structure-aware optimizers have been the focus of recent study for the optimization of parameters in variational quantum circuits. Many of these optimizers follow a coordinate-based paradigm, making single parameter updates by using classical approximations to the cost function generated from quantum sampling. However, the performance of structure-aware optimizers on real quantum hardware at large system size has yet to be demonstrated. candidates.abstract: Two-photon lithography (TPL) prints three-dimensional polymer architectures with sub-diffraction features, but writing them voxel by voxel limits its throughput. This review examines how parallelization overcomes this limit with fixed multi-focus arrays, reconfigurable holography using spatial light modulators and digital micromirror devices, hybrid metalens arrays, shaped beams, temporally focused projection and two-step absorption. Published systems reach peak rates above $10^{8}$ voxels s$^{-1}$ with scanned focus arrays and up to $1.7\times10^{9}$ voxels s$^{-1}$ with grayscale projection under a fine-voxel definition, and parallel features as small as 20-55 nm.
